title: A Drama on the Family Radio
description: Recall spoken-word radio entertainment through a script, sound effects, and the people performing at a microphone.
cardDescription: Recall spoken-word radio entertainment through a script, sound effects, and the people performing at a microphone.
subtheme: A Drama on the Family Radio
focus: A radio drama tells its story through voices and sound. The clues separate performers, written cues, and the equipment carrying the broadcast.
solvingTip: Use what is heard or spoken rather than a visible film image.
words: RADIO
Broadcast medium carrying a drama through sound alone
SERIAL
Story presented in successive continuing installments
SCRIPT
Written words and directions for a radio performance
MICROPHONE
Device converting performers' sounds into an electrical signal
ANNOUNCER
Voice introducing a broadcast or identifying a program
ACTOR
Performer speaking a character's part in a drama
CUE
Signal telling a performer when to enter or speak
VOICE
Human sound carrying a character's words
SCENE
One portion of the drama's action
EFFECT
Created sound suggesting an action or setting
DIAL
Tuning control on a traditional home receiver
TUNE
To adjust a receiver to a broadcast station
SOUND
Audible material from which the drama is made
CAST
Group of performers taking the story's parts

answerNotes.RADIO: A radio drama relies on voices, music, and effects rather than a screen image.
answerNotes.SERIAL: A serial continues a narrative across episodes, unlike a completely unrelated story each time.
answerNotes.SCRIPT: A script contains dialogue and cues; it is different from the final sound heard by listeners.
answerNotes.MICROPHONE: A microphone takes sound in, while a loudspeaker converts a signal back into audible sound.
answerNotes.ANNOUNCER: The announcer introduces or links parts of a broadcast rather than necessarily playing a story character.

title: An Evening of Vaudeville
description: Explore a traditional variety bill through its short acts, entertainers, and theater spaces.
cardDescription: Explore a traditional variety bill through its short acts, entertainers, and theater spaces.
focus: Vaudeville combined separate acts in one program. A comic sketch, a musical turn, and a balancing feat could share a bill without forming one continuous story.
solvingTip: Separate a performer, an act, and a place beside the stage.
words: VAUDEVILLE
Theatrical variety entertainment made up of separate short acts
ACROBAT
Performer demonstrating balancing or tumbling skills
JUGGLER
Entertainer keeping several objects in controlled moving patterns
SKIT
Short comic scene performed as part of a variety program
BILL
Program listing the acts in a theater show
ACT
One separate performance in a variety show
STAGE
Raised area where the entertainers perform
WING
Side area concealed from the theater audience
SONG
Vocal musical number on a variety bill
DANCE
Rhythmic movement presented by a performer
COMIC
Entertainer whose act aims to make an audience laugh
CURTAIN
Hanging screen separating the stage from the auditorium
BOW
Acknowledgment made by a performer after an act
PROP
Object used by a performer during a stage act

answerNotes.VAUDEVILLE: Vaudeville describes a form of variety programming, not one single dramatic plot.
answerNotes.ACROBAT: An acrobat's act emphasizes physical skill rather than spoken dialogue alone.
answerNotes.JUGGLER: A juggler may use balls, clubs, or other objects; the definition concerns the skill rather than one prop.
answerNotes.SKIT: A skit is one brief piece, while the entire bill includes several acts.
answerNotes.BILL: Bill has a theatrical meaning here rather than meaning an invoice.

title: Song and Dance in a Movie Musical
description: Explore a film musical through its singing, repeated tunes, dances, and recorded accompaniment.
cardDescription: Explore a film musical through its singing, repeated tunes, dances, and recorded accompaniment.
subtheme: Song and Dance in a Movie Musical
focus: A musical integrates songs with its story or presentation. The clues distinguish a sung part, a returning musical number, and the technical work of pairing picture with sound.
solvingTip: Use whether the definition asks for words, music, movement, or recording work.
words: MUSICAL
Film genre featuring songs as part of its presentation or story
REPRISE
Return of a previously heard song or musical passage
CHORUS
Group singing together, or a recurring part of a song
LYRIC
One word-based line or the verbal text of a song
PLAYBACK
Reproduction of recorded sound used during or after filming
DUET
Song performed by two singers together
DANCE
Movement set to the musical number's rhythm
SCORE
Written or composed music accompanying a film
VOICE
Sound produced by a singing performer
STEP
Single movement in a dance sequence
TUNE
Melody carried by a familiar song
SET
Constructed location used for filming a number
DUB
To add or replace recorded sound for a film
SCENE
One part of the movie's unfolding action

answerNotes.MUSICAL: A musical combines performance with a film narrative or sequence; not every movie containing background music is called a musical.
answerNotes.REPRISE: A reprise brings earlier material back, sometimes with a changed setting or meaning.
answerNotes.CHORUS: The film context can use chorus for performers or a repeated song section.
answerNotes.LYRIC: Lyric concerns the words, while melody describes their musical tune.
answerNotes.PLAYBACK: Playback uses an existing recording; it differs from making the original recording.

title: A Western on the Movie Screen
description: Identify the familiar props, roles, and landscape words of a classic Western film scene.
cardDescription: Identify the familiar props, roles, and landscape words of a classic Western film scene.
subtheme: A Western on the Movie Screen
focus: These clues concern film conventions rather than a complete history of the American West. A costume piece, a riding tool, and a character role have separate names.
solvingTip: Use the object’s purpose or where it is worn before trying the story-role words.
words: WESTERN
Film genre commonly associated with frontier settings and horseback travel
LARIAT
Looped rope used for catching livestock in a riding scene
SHERIFF
County law officer often portrayed with a badge in a Western
SADDLE
Rider's seat fastened on a horse's back
POSSE
Group assembled to assist a law officer in a familiar Western plot
HORSE
Animal carrying a rider through the film's landscape
SPUR
Metal riding aid worn at the heel of a boot
RANCH
Livestock property appearing in many Western settings
BADGE
Insignia identifying a film law officer
HAT
Headwear often given a broad brim in the genre
VEST
Sleeveless garment worn over a shirt in many Western costumes
DUST
Fine dry particles rising behind a traveling horse
STUNT
Performed action requiring special physical skill for a film
SALOON
Drinking establishment familiar in Western movie settings

answerNotes.WESTERN: Western names a film genre; its conventions should not be treated as a complete historical account.
answerNotes.LARIAT: A lariat is a rope tool, distinct from the saddle or bridle on the horse.
answerNotes.SHERIFF: Sheriff is an office with real duties; films may simplify how the role works.
answerNotes.SADDLE: A saddle supports the rider, while reins help communicate direction through the bridle.
answerNotes.POSSE: Posse has a law-enforcement meaning in this scene rather than simply naming any group of friends.

title: Clues in a Mystery Film
description: Follow a fictional investigation through motives, suspect accounts, and misleading pieces of evidence.
cardDescription: Follow a fictional investigation through motives, suspect accounts, and misleading pieces of evidence.
focus: A mystery story can withhold information until its solution. The clues name storytelling and investigation terms, distinguishing a reason for an action from an account of someone’s whereabouts.
solvingTip: Match the question being answered: why, where, who, or what might mislead the investigator.
words: WHODUNIT
Mystery story centered on discovering who committed an act
ALIBI
Account or evidence placing a suspect elsewhere at the relevant time
MOTIVE
Reason a fictional suspect might have for an action
SLEUTH
Informal word for a detective in a mystery story
REDHERRING
Misleading story clue, with spaces omitted
CLUE
Detail that may help solve the film's central puzzle
SUSPECT
Person considered as a possible participant in the mystery
CASE
Investigation at the center of a detective story
LEAD
Promising line of inquiry followed by an investigator
NOTE
Written message discovered during the story
KEY
Object or important idea that helps unlock the solution
CODE
System hiding a message's ordinary meaning
PLOT
Sequence of events making up the mystery
REVEAL
Moment when a hidden fact is disclosed

answerNotes.WHODUNIT: Whodunit is a story-category word formed from a spoken question; it is not the name of the investigator.
answerNotes.ALIBI: An alibi addresses whereabouts, while a motive concerns a possible reason for an action.
answerNotes.MOTIVE: Motive is different from proof that an action occurred or that a particular person performed it.
answerNotes.SLEUTH: Sleuth names the investigator, rather than the person being investigated.
answerNotes.REDHERRING: Red herring is written continuously in the grid; it describes a diversion rather than a literal fish in the plot.
